newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says BOE on way to full independence.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says BOE on way to full independence.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Wednesday Britain's moves to give greater independence to its central bank were a step in the right direction toward full independence for the Bank of England.
A spokesman read out the following statement from the central bank president in response to Reuter enquiries:
"I have noted with interest the importance the British government is placing on independence of the central bank for the stability of the currency.
"If I interpret this correctly the new regulation is to be seen as a step on the way to full independence in line with the Maastricht Treaty," he added.
Gordon Brown, Britain's new chancellor of the exchequer, said on Tuesday that the Bank of England would in future be free to set interest rate levels.
But the decision fell short of the Maastricht Treaty's requirement for full autonomy, as Britain's Treasury retains the right to set inflation targets for the central bank.
Full central bank independence is one of the requirements laid down in the Maastricht Treaty for countries that wish to enter the single European currency.
Although the BOE move was seen as a step toward meeting this requirement, Britain is widely expected not to join the single currency at its launch in 1999.
